missedOpportunities.moment: Turn 3, the opening response 'I think the problem is COGS', given before any framework.
missedOpportunities.betterResponse: Our goal is to explain why net margin fell from 24% to 6% while revenue grew 15%, and then find levers to restore it. I'd split profit into revenue and costs. On revenue: price per item, transaction volume and product mix. On costs: COGS (beans, dairy, food, packaging), labor, occupancy and overhead, and other. Because revenue grew while margin collapsed, my hypothesis is that costs, likely COGS, outpaced prices. So I'd start by comparing each cost line as a percent of revenue two years ago versus today.

I'd also want to know whether competitors are seeing the same squeeze.

before.topFix: Open by restating the objective and laying out a complete profit tree before naming an answer. Then present any hypothesis as testable: give the reasoning plus the specific data you'd ask for (e.g., cost lines as a percent of revenue then versus now, and menu price changes). That way, when challenged, you can point to the test instead of falling back on 'I just feel like.'
